assets.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: standalone dominant website hero photograph for a British vehicle-adaptation specialist; AI marketing illustration with fictional people.
Primary request: Edit and outpaint the supplied actual Jeff Gosling hand-controls catalogue photograph into a photorealistic scene of TWO technicians actively installing or precisely adjusting those hand controls. This must unmistakably depict installation work, with a small hex key touching a real mounting fastener.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, not merely inspiration. Preserve its BMW right-hand-drive dashboard and steering wheel, and its exact distinctive textured cylindrical push-pull hand-control grip on the bent black lever at the lower right of the wheel. Keep the grip geometry, lever shape, bracket, steering-column mounting position, and completed mechanism intact, crisp, mechanically plausible and recognisable. Do not replace it with a generic adaptation, gear lever, joystick, or invented assembly.
Scene/backdrop: widen the view outward through the open RIGHT driver door into a tidy specialist workshop with clean neutral surfaces, calm natural British daylight and only subdued background equipment. The car is stationary.
Subject/action: one believable adult technician in plain navy workwear crouches naturally just OUTSIDE the open driver's doorway, leaning in purposefully. Their face and upper body are visible. They use a small hex key in one hand to fit/adjust a mounting fastener beneath and to the right of the steering column, while the other hand steadies the existing bracket. Hands only partly cover the fastener area; the distinctive control grip and most of its black bent lever remain fully visible. A second believable adult technician in plain navy workwear stands naturally outside behind the crouching technician, holding a compact work light that illuminates the mounting point and watching the work attentively. Both have visible faces and convincing purposeful working posture.
Composition/framing: a single wide landscape photograph, 1792x1024. View across the open driver's doorway showing the recognisable wheel and hand controls with the technicians alongside. Keep both faces, the working hands, hex key and control hardware within the central 80% of image width AND middle 65% of image height, with breathing room above and below for a roughly 2:1 responsive crop. Hardware and work are the focal point. Keep all anatomy believable and bodies outside the footwell; no person sits awkwardly beneath the steering wheel.
Style/lighting: premium but natural documentary workshop photography, realistic skin texture, ordinary authentic-looking people, navy fabric texture, soft daylight, balanced neutral whites and subdued blue accents, crisp adaptation hardware, gentle background separation, no glossy stock-photo posing. Their expressions are focused on the fitting task, not smiling at the camera.
Constraints: preserve the source car interior and actual hand control as faithfully as possible while adding technicians and surrounding context. Keep secure intact mounting and believable tool contact. No sparks, fictional wiring, disassembled steering wheel, extra mechanical rods, extra limbs or fingers. No added branding, signs, written text, watermarks, badges, captions or claims. Existing inherent factory details on the preserved car need not be invented or amplified. Produce ONE standalone photograph, not a collage.
review_notes: Two technicians visibly work at the open right driver door: crouching technician applies a small hex key; second technician holds a work light.
Source BMW steering wheel and distinctive textured hand-control grip with bent black lever remain clearly recognisable and unobstructed.
Generator returned 1660x948 (approximately 16:9) despite a 1792x1024 request. Original is preserved without resizing.
Second technician's hair reaches the upper image edge; preview a 2:1 crop to keep her face comfortable. No obvious key-invariant failure found.
